metaData.originalTitle: Q&A: How KRAFTON Built PUBG Ally， a Co-Playable Character Powered by NVIDIA ACE
metaData.title: Q&A: How KRAFTON Built PUBG Ally， a Co-Playable Character Powered by NVIDIA ACE
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: KRAFTON details how they built PUBG Ally, a co-playable character powered by NVIDIA ACE, using on-device ASR, a 2B-parameter small language model, and TTS for real-time, grounded AI teammates.
metaData.summary: In this Q&A, KRAFTON's research lead and project manager explain the architecture and design decisions behind PUBG Ally, an AI teammate for PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS that runs entirely on-device using NVIDIA ACE. The system combines automatic speech recognition, a quantized Mistral-NeMo-Minitron-2B small language model (SLM), and custom text-to-speech. Key engineering choices include running the SLM locally to avoid network latency, implementing a System 1/System 2 separation (behavior tree for reactive actions, language model for intent and speech), and constraining the game world to a single map and fixed item taxonomy for tractable domain adaptation. PUBG Ally supports English, Korean, and Chinese, uses teacher-student distillation for domain-specific knowledge, and includes structured long-term memory that persists across matches. The interviews also cover testing methodologies for non-deterministic AI, advice for other studios, and future directions for co-playable characters.

mainPoints.point: PUBG Ally is a co-playable character (CPC) distinct from NPCs, designed to cooperate and adapt via natural voice interaction.
mainPoints.explanation: Unlike scripted bots, the CPC uses ASR + SLM + TTS to understand player intent, reason about game state, and respond dynamically in real time, aiming to feel like a real squadmate.

mainPoints.point: A local 2B-parameter SLM was chosen over cloud LLMs to meet latency constraints and fit within GPU VRAM headroom.
mainPoints.explanation: Cloud round-trips were too slow for live squad communication. The quantized Mistral-NeMo-Minitron-2B runs on GPUs with as low as 8GB VRAM, providing responsive, predictable response times.

mainPoints.point: A System 1/System 2 architecture separates reactive gameplay from language reasoning.
mainPoints.explanation: A behavior tree handles fast actions (movement, combat) at game tick rate, while the language model handles deliberate tasks (interpreting intent, generating speech). Reflex-level actions never wait on the model.

mainPoints.point: Domain adaptation was achieved by constraining the game world, teacher-student distillation, and agentic grounding in live engine state.
mainPoints.explanation: KRAFTON limited scope to one map and a fixed item taxonomy, used a teacher model to generate grounded responses, and distilled those behaviors into the on-device SLM. Ally fetches real-time game data via tool calls to stay accurate.

mainPoints.point: Structured long-term memory lets Ally remember players across matches, enhancing perceived companionship.
mainPoints.explanation: Long-term memory stores player profiles, preferred weapons, and past match results. Short-term memory handles within-match context. Player feedback showed that cross-match memory turned Ally from a per-match assistant into an ongoing teammate.

keyQuotes: We treat this as a System 1 / System 2 problem, analogous to the fast, instinctive responses and the slower, deliberate reasoning in human decision-making.
The goal is the player's experience, which boils down to whether the companion feels like a good teammate.
If we could give just one piece of advice, it would be to get that loop running early, and to keep it cheap enough to run often.
one player asked Ally to look out for a Beryl in the first match, and from the next match onward Ally started finding it without being asked.
